en: The Great Dhāraṇī Divine Spell Sūtra Spoken by the Seven Buddhas and Eight Bodhisattvas, Scroll One.
Translated during the Jin Dynasty; the name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost, now appended to the Catalogue of the Eastern Jin.
The first, Vipaśyin Buddha,
stated that there are eighteen thousand illnesses,
all of which he has completely cured with a single incantation.
This dhāraṇī is named *Suloduha* (in the Jin language, "Definitive Brahma-Sound").

*Cibazhou cibazhou*, *hunubazhou hunubazhou*, *fuliubazhou fuliubazhou*, *cibazhou cibazhou*, *ejuebazhou ejuebazhou*, *dohunabazhou*, *shamenubazhou*, *huxiubazhou*, *mijihunabazhou*, *yihudina dinabazhou*, *milidina dinabazhou*, *shaerudina dinabazhou*, *mijianudina dinabazhou*, *yuzhadoudina dinabazhou*. *Svāhā*. Recite this mantra three times.
Tie fourteen knots with yellow thread;
recite the mantra once for each knot and fasten them around the neck.
By the power of this dhāraṇī, all [obstacles] can be utterly subdued.
He can move mountains, cut off rivers, and dry up the great ocean;
he can crush all mountains into fine dust like motes of pollen;
and even if the sun and moon lose their course, he can cause them to proceed correctly.
They are fully capable of averting calamities;
when wind and rain are out of season, they can cause them to fall at the proper times;
and when grain does not ripen, they can cause it to be abundant and mature.
Invasions by neighboring states can all be repelled;
the evil intentions of ministers who plot rebellion will immediately be extinguished;
and the calamities of epidemics and disasters can all be warded off.
When pestilence demons enter a country, this can expel them;
when the kalpa of war and weapons arises, this can destroy it.
The power of this dhāraṇī is immeasurable and boundless in its ability to avert calamities and eliminate anomalies.
Were it to be explained in detail, it would not be exhausted even at the end of an eon.
These dhāraṇī phrases are divine mantras spoken by seventy-two billion Buddhas.
The second formula is a dhāraṇī spoken by the Buddha named *Hu-sū-duō* (Husuda), which in the Jin language means "Eliminating All Heat and Affliction.
These dhāraṇī phrases are divine mantras spoken by seventy-two billion Buddhas.

Dhamate na, chavate na, śaphu-śaphu-te na, usuta-usuta-te na, phupha-śa-phupha-śa-te na, aśute ayute-te na, niri-ccha-niri-ccha-te na, cibhau-cibhau-te na, sukhatau sukhatau-te na, yamukha-yamukha-te na, śabhu-te na, ośabhu-te na, susabhu-te na, śaprabhu-te na. Svāhā. (Recite this mantra three times.)
Tie three knots with yellow thread around one's neck.
By the spiritual power of this dhāraṇī,
it can cause the trichiliocosm to shake in six ways.
Mountains, rivers, rocks, and cliffs surged and submerged with great majesty;
all sentient beings therein conceived the aspiration for unexcelled bodhicitta,
whereby they were able to eliminate the heavy karmic offenses of birth and death accumulated over seven thousand koṭis of kalpas.
The sickness and suffering of all sentient beings will be extinguished without remainder.
Among them, any sentient being who writes down, recites, or even hears the name of a single phrase of this dhāraṇī shall,
for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges-sands of world-ages, [attain...]
The heavy karmic obstacles shall be crushed and extinguished without remainder.
The third divine mantra spoken by the Buddha Anupamarāja is called *Mṛgī-dhū*—in the Jin language, "Golden Drum.
It [destroys] all the karmic obstacles, retributive obstacles, and the heavy defilements of the afflictive obstacles possessed by sentient beings.
One is able to utterly destroy them all without remainder:

*pūludina*, *yānautkhina*, *aṅgautkhina*, *yānautkhina*, *caphuphukhina*, *yānautkhina*, *uśaphuphukhina*, *yānautkhina*, *śambhūbhūkhiṇa*, *kaurīṭabhūbhūkhiṇa*, *cipatukhiṇa*, *yānadhunakhiṇa*, *uśabhūkhiṇa*, *cadūriṇa*, *khiṇasvāhā*. Recite this mantra seven times.
Tie four knots with yellow thread around the neck.
These dhāraṇī phrases were spoken by as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
If there are those who copy, read, or recite this dhāraṇī,
all their heavy evils and most severe karmic obstructions from kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges shall be [eliminated].
Furthermore, the five heinous crimes and the offenses of the icchantikas shall all be extinguished without remainder;
as shall all other heavy sins of sentient beings,
including the defilements that obstruct the Path and the defilements of karma.
Upon hearing what they preach, [all afflictions] are extinguished without remainder.
Wherever those who copy, read, or recite it may go—
whether to kingdoms, cities, towns, villages, mountain forests, or burial mounds— [the same shall occur].
Among those sentient beings, anyone who hears the name of this dhāraṇī even once will,
after the end of their life, all attain rebirth in the land of Akṣobhya Buddha;
furthermore, until they achieve Buddhahood, they shall not fall into the three miserable realms.
To perform this dhāraṇī rite, on the sixteenth day of the fourth month, one should enter an east-facing stūpa and circumambulate it eighty times during the day. Then,
standing facing east beneath the western wall of the stūpa, one should proceed.
Recite the mantra twenty-four times.
One must not sleep for seven days and seven nights.
Seven lamps of sesame oil must be prepared and placed at the four corners.
Having bathed thoroughly and cleanly, put on new, pure garments,
and abstain from alcohol, meat, and the five pungent herbs for one day and one night.
At that time, I shall manifest before that person and emit a great radiance;
with my golden hand, I will stroke the crown of their head and immediately bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment.
All the karmic obstructions and defilements of this person shall be extinguished without remainder.
The great dhāraṇī spoken by the fourth Buddha, Krakucchanda, is named Vajradhvaja-samādhi;
it is capable of healing and transforming sentient beings within the five turbidities of the triple world.
It can completely eliminate all evil afflictions, sores, and grave illnesses,
as well as all karmic obstructions, retributive obstructions,
and the various stains of afflictive obstructions.
*Dhyānadhūḥ* (in the Jin language: "Gathering in sentient beings' suffering and causing them to emerge from the mire of craving and desire").
Those who hear this are liberated from the three defilements: greed, hatred, and pride.
*Ajñāna-hetu*. Day.
Inapari-dina-hejju-gi-bu-arya-dina-hejju-paśa-hejju.
Cchāpūrmāhiddho ajñāhiddho jño vā no hiddho.
Ogīndramahi, jogīpudramahi, jodhāndulināhi, jodha.
Pulināhe zhòu āhūhùruò hézhòu fúlìdìnàhézhòu.
Svāhā dhyānaṭa-mūlide (in the Jin language: "Great Abundance and Fulfillment") jībumunī huḥ, koṭamunī huḥ.
Mūliṇu-bhūbhū-hū śa-ya-to-bhūbhū-hū chi-pu-bhūbhū-hū.
Aṅgīrasa pūpūhu bharide na pūpūhu svāhā. Recite this mantra once;
tie thirteen knots with yellow thread and fasten it around the neck.
All the dharani phrases mentioned above and those spoken by me were all taught by ninety-nine billion Buddhas of the past. Should there be anyone who reads,
recites, or transcribes them, [they shall obtain great merit].
In this present life, one shall attain the Vajradhvaja Samādhi;
all fetters and afflictions will be utterly destroyed without remainder,
and the suffering of sentient beings shall be uprooted.
The sovereign spiritual powers described above are immeasurable and limitless.
The fifth Buddha, Kanakamuni, wishing to proclaim the name of the Great Dharani called *Pibhyo*—which in the Jin language means "Sound Resonating Throughout the Ten Directions"—[spoke as follows].
There were none who did not submit and take refuge.
He awakened sentient beings like the roll of thunder,
causing those mired in ignorance to attain the eye of wisdom.
This dharani phrase was spoken by seventy-seven hundred million Buddhas of the past; I now speak it:

Cana-radi-na | Anaki-anan | Usaki-anan | Dhunaki-anan | Avritiki-anan | Kshayananaki-anan | Kimbara-ditanaki-anan | Mitiki-ditanaki-anan | Arandiki-ditanavi-anan | Hupadi-tanaki-lan-an | Mitikidutan | Jyuan-adi-tan | U-u-u-u-hadi-tan | Chibupapadi-tan | Svaha. Recite this mantra three times.
Tie three knots with yellow thread at the site of the pain;
by the power of this dhāraṇī,
it can cause the trichiliocosm to shake in six ways.
Among all those sentient beings therein,
anyone who hears these dharani phrases but once, even by the ear,
shall [be spared] for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of kalpas.
All grave offenses, including the five heinous crimes of immediate retribution, shall be extinguished without remainder.
If there are sentient beings who practice and recite this,
reducing their sleep for seven days and seven nights, [their transgressions will be purified].
That person, in their present body, attains the Lion-King Samādhi;
hundreds of thousands of Buddhas appear before them and bestow predictions of enlightenment.
Furthermore, the neighboring kingdoms and powerful enemies of that land [shall submit].
When they intended to invade and oppress the king,
at that time he, together with his various ministers,
bathed himself clean and put on new, pure garments.
On the high tower, according to their respective directions,
one should first pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions,
and thereafter pay homage to me, Kāśyapa Buddha.
Recite my name three times while burning incense and scattering flowers;
at that time, recite the dhāraṇī verses.
By the majestic spiritual power of this dhāraṇī, [the desired result shall be attained].
Mahābrahmā, Śakra, and the Four Great Kings rained down swords and blades from the midst of the void,
while great black winds arose from all four directions.
He shall cause all his troops to be unable to see the light of the sun or moon;
the hosts of yakṣas shall suck away their vital essence,
so that none may escape and they naturally retreat and disperse.
Such is the majestic spiritual power of this great dhāraṇī.
The sixth Buddha, Kāśyapa, was about to preach the name of the great dhāraṇī, *Cūḍāmaṇi*, which in the Jin language means "Rescuing and Delivering All Sentient Beings."
Escape from the suffering of birth and death.

*Ajñātevarīde*, *Cāpotevarīde*, *Uṣaṇevarīde*, *Śākharetevarīde*, *Huśaduparīde*, *Devavarīde*, *Nahuparīdevarīde*, *Najipulaparīdevarīde*, *Nahutaretevarīde*, *Prajñāparīdevarīde*, *Napaduretevarīde*, *Śaryamitundatevarīde*. *Svāhā*. Recite this mantra seven times.
Tie six knots with a yellow thread at the site of pain.
These dhāraṇī phrases were spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas of the past.
By the power of this dhāraṇī,
it can cause ten billion buddha-worlds to quake in six ways;
all mountains, rivers, and rocky walls are utterly shattered into atoms like fine dust.
It became a single Buddha-world;
all things therein were transformed into a golden color,
so vast and boundless that nothing else could be seen.
One sees only golden color and no other colors;
by the power of this dhāraṇī,
it is able to [benefit] the sentient beings of a hundred buddha-worlds.
All heavy karmic offenses from past lives and the sufferings of the three miserable realms shall be extinguished without remainder.
Among those sentient beings who practice and recite this dhāraṇī,
there are none who have not yet resolved to attain unsurpassed bodhicitta.
They shall all be caused to resolve their minds for enlightenment and reach the stage of non-retrogression.
Those who have already resolved their minds and practice this dhāraṇī shall transcend the seventh bhūmi and proceed to the tenth bhūmi.
This is the Great Emptiness Liberation Gate of the Vajra Samādhi Dhāraṇī.
From the first generation of the mind of enlightenment, when Bodhisattvas practice this samādhi,
they never fail to enter the Vajra-samādhi beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment until the very end.
The seventh is Śākyamuni Buddha, who wishes to proclaim a great dhāraṇī named *Uṣṇīṣavijayā*— translated into the Jin language as "Golden Light Radiance"—
which eliminates the darkness, obscurity, and stagnation of sentient beings within the three realms and rescues them from their perils and hardships.
These dharani phrases were spoken by ninety-nine billion Buddhas of the past; I now speak them:

*Girudunadi naṭi* | *Bhigidi naṭi* | *Usuhudi naṭi* | *Gimuda naṭi* | *Yanodu naṭi* | *Aryapadu naṭi* | *Yapadu naṭi* | *Gimuparya naṭi* | *Ushaphu naṭi* | *Migisudu naṭi* | *Yamigidi naṭi* | *Ponumi naṭi* | *Biliditha naṭi* | *Svāhā*. Recite this mantra fourteen times.
Tie fourteen knots with yellow thread at the site of pain;
by the power of this dhāraṇī,
it can cause the trichiliocosm to shake in six ways.
Among those sentient beings, those whose karmic defilements from past lives had entangled,
enveloped, and bound them, remaining in dark obscurity,
heard this dhāraṇī but once as it reached their ears.
All shall attain rebirth in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
As for those practitioners who receive, uphold, recite, and transcribe this dhāraṇī,
those who have not yet resolved their minds toward awakening shall all be inspired to do so and reach the stage of firm resolve.
Those who first resolve their minds enter the stream of the Dharma;
by abiding equally in the eighth stage, they swiftly reach the ground of Buddhahood through the power of this dhāraṇī.
In a single leap, they transcend to beneath the Bodhi tree,
proceeding even unto the stage of Buddhahood to sit at the site of enlightenment.
This samādhi is named the King of Golden Light Samādhi.
Awakening all sentient beings, they leap forth from the three realms;
uprooting all calamities and surpassing all the multitude of sages, they swiftly attain the path of Buddhahood.
If there are sentient beings who wish to practice this dhāraṇī, [they shall do so].
If one wishes to manifest the four fruits of śrāmaṇya in this very body,

and desires to eliminate the obstacles to the Path— namely the five heinous crimes and the violation of the four grave prohibitions— accumulated over hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas in the past;
One should practice this dhāraṇī so as to eradicate [all afflictions] in the present life without leaving a single remnant.
For twenty-one days— three times seven— one should maintain the prohibitive precepts (śīla) as if they were a bright pearl.
For one day and one night, practice the Way and repent during the six periods;
bathe thoroughly to ensure purity, don new and clean robes, and employ flowers of seven colors and three kinds of famous incense.
One should make offerings and scatter [flowers] before Śākyamuni Buddha,
prostrate oneself fully before the stupa of his relics, and repent with self-reproach.
At that time, one should recite these dhāraṇī phrases eighty-one times, doing so every day in this manner.
If not attained within seven days, they shall attain it on the second week, and even by the third week.
All heavy sins committed throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of *koṭis* of kalpas will be extinguished without remainder.
The Buddhas of the ten directions emit great rays of light that touch his body;
at that time, this person’s mind and heart are filled with joy,
just like a bhikṣu who has attained the third dhyāna.
At that time, Mahābrahmā, Śakra-devendra, and the Four Great Kings will immediately bestow upon them the four fruits of śrāmaṇya.

The *Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra* states: "The adornment of the Mahāyāna necklace consists of the fourfold discipline, concentration, and wisdom, and the unsurpassed dhāraṇī; therefore, one should properly maintain the precepts."
Precepts can produce concentration, and concentration can produce wisdom.
The first dharani taught by Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva is named Jambumati; in the Jin language, it means "Liberating the Bonds of Sentient Beings."
Now all sufferings of illness have been entirely eliminated;
one is able to ward off obstacles to the Path and extract the arrows of the three poisons,
while the ninety-eight latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) gradually fade away.
Crossing over the three streams of existence, may one manifest in this body to attain the Way.

Jipudunadì, Yánfóuzhinadì, Sūchúbùzhinadì, Zhùqíbùzhinadì, Wūsūdūzhinadì, Pōzhébùzhinadì, Shāmólàichángzhinadì, Āshǔpólàichángzhinadì, Rúbādìzhinadì. Svāhā. Recite this mantra three times; tie five-colored thread into two knots and fasten them around the neck.
This dhāraṇī was spoken by forty-two billion Buddhas.
If there are practitioners who are able to copy, read, or recite this dhāraṇī, they shall,
in their present life, be protected by a thousand Buddhas.
After this person’s life has ended, they shall not fall into the evil realms;
they will be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven above to behold Maitreya.
Furthermore, there are sentient beings who are able to practice this dhāraṇī.
Fast for seven days, consuming only cow’s milk;
eat a single meal at midday with no other food.
For one day and one night, perform repentance during the six periods.

By paying homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions and repenting for the transgressions committed, all heavy offenses accumulated over billions of *koṭis* of kalpas are entirely extinguished at once;
even those offenses resulting from the violation of the precepts in various ways are likewise completely eliminated.
The calamities and evils of the five heinous crimes, as well as those of the icchantikas,
shall all be extinguished through earnest and profound repentance. This should be performed ten times during each of the six periods of the day within a secluded and quiet room, or inside a stupa.
If this person’s mind is pure and sincere,
I shall go to their place at that time;
because they see me, their mind will become even more pure and sincere.
Because their minds are pure and profound, they shall behold a thousand Buddhas.
The Buddhas will stroke their heads with their hands and immediately bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment.
Their past karmic offenses and evils shall be forever extinguished without remainder.
Second, I, the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, wish to proclaim a great dhāraṇī named Anaghiyau, which in the Jin language means "extracting the suffering of sentient beings.
It is uniquely transcendent within the three realms and peerless.
If there are sentient beings who, tossed by waves through the six realms of existence, have no one able to save them, I shall rescue them and cause them to escape their hardships.

Tie fourteen knots with a five-colored thread around both wrists.
These dhāraṇī phrases were spoken by seventy-two billion Buddhas of the past.
I have now finished speaking;
it is for the sake of protecting the True Dharma, for the sake of delivering sentient beings,
and so that all practitioners may achieve success through the myriad practices.
It is for the sake of causing those śrāvakas who have not yet realized the fruit to attain it;
and for the sake of causing pratyekabuddhas to cross the great river of the twelve links of dependent origination and rescue all living beings.
This dharani is taught so that the vows and fruits of all bodhisattvas may be fulfilled, from their first generation of the mind of awakening up to the tenth stage.
Furthermore, by the power of this dharani—
It can cause all sentient beings within the trichiliocosm who dwell in dark and hidden places, as well as those suffering in the three miserable realms, [to be liberated].
Upon hearing this dhāraṇī but once, it enters the range of one’s ears and one attains the knowledge of past lives;
even up to fourteen lifetimes, one shall attain complete liberation.
If there are good sons or good daughters who...
Those who wish to practice this dhāraṇī should,
for twenty-one days, bathe themselves to purify, put on new and clean garments,
and [practice] either within a stūpa or in a pure location.
In the latter part of the night, when the morning star has appeared, speak thus to this Great Morning Star:
"Speak for me to the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja.
Say this three times.
"May my root offenses be removed"—thus three times.
"May my offenses that obstruct the Path be removed"—thus three times.
"Grant me the four fruits of the śramaṇa"—thus three times.
At that time, I immediately went to his place;
standing before that person, I bestowed upon him the four fruits of śrāmaṇya.
"I vow to grant [this]," I said three times in this manner.
Burn aloeswood incense.
If one dreams of obtaining an āmalaka fruit,
or obtaining a harītakī fruit.
If one obtains a *bimbara* fruit,
or a *vibhitaka* fruit, or an apricot and the like,
at that time one should apply oneself with diligent vigor.
Whether it be [an image of] a chicken egg or a fist,
at that time one should recite the mantra seven times when the morning star appears;
if the mind is favorable, one should further recite it seven times.
The Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha constantly travels through various lands to enable all practitioners to attain the myriad practices.
Third, I, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, wish to proclaim a great dhāraṇī named Anagijñāpāramitā; in the Jin language, this means "Great Deliverance."
May it pervade all infinite sentient beings of the ten directions.

Oṣadīna | Jinajinadīna | Bukadudīna | Naśubhridīna | Amabhubhridīna | Oṣaṇāṭadīna | Gibūbūdīna | Gidudu-dhudīna | Jyapamunāladīna | Ojugunāladīna | Jyapapunāladīna | Jambūbūladīna | Svāhā. Recite this mantra five times.
Tie twenty-four knots made from thread of five colors around the neck;
these dhāraṇī phrases were spoken by ninety-nine billion buddhas of the past.
For all practitioners who cultivate the six perfections but have not yet resolved their minds [for enlightenment],
and for all śrāvakas who have not yet realized the fruits [of their practice], the Buddhas act as their guides.
If there are any seers and immortals within this trichiliocosm who have not yet resolved to attain unsurpassed bodhicitta,
may they all be caused to resolve their minds upon it.
There are ordinary beings who have not yet attained faith;
by means of seeds, I cause the sprouts of the Dharma to grow through the majestic spiritual power of this dhāraṇī.
And by the power of my skillful means,
I cause all that they cultivate to be fully accomplished,
as well as within this trichiliocosm.
Sentient beings who are in secluded obscurity, darkness, or stagnation, as well as those in the three miserable realms—
all who hear this *dhāraṇī* of mine shall be delivered from suffering. Furthermore,
those Bodhisattvas who have not yet attained the first stage (*bhūmi*) [shall also be benefited].
They cause them to attain the first stage;
they cause them to attain the stages in succession up to the tenth stage.
Having already attained these successive levels of the ten bhūmis, they...
By virtue of having attained the power of this dhāraṇī,
in a single moment of thought one proceeds directly to the stage of Buddhahood;
the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics naturally reach full maturity.
If a śrāvaka hears this dhāraṇī even once, and having read, recited, copied,
and practiced this dhāraṇī, abides in accordance with the Dharma with a straightforward mind, [he shall attain such benefits].
The four fruits of śrāmaṇya are attained without seeking,
by the power of this dhāraṇī; thus,
throughout the trichiliocosm.
He can cause the mountains, rivers, rocky cliffs, and the waters of the four great oceans to surge and boil;
he can reduce Mount Sumeru and the Iron Ring Mountains to mere motes of dust,
causing all sentient beings therein to resolve upon unsurpassed bodhicitta.
There are bodhisattvas and śrāvakas who practice the path;
if they encounter obstacles that hinder their progress or are afflicted by suffering and illness,
I shall rescue them all and cause them to escape these perils.
May all that they cultivate be fully accomplished.
If there are sentient beings who seek their aspirations in the present life and practice this dhāraṇī, [may it be so].
For twenty-one days— three periods of seven days— he purely maintained the ground of the precepts;
day and night, during the six periods, he practiced the Way,
burning various famous incenses and scattering flowers of five colors.
One should repent before the ten directions, reproaching oneself for one's transgressions.
From the limits of birth and death to the limits of birth and death, one should reproach oneself with shame and remorse.
At that time, one should invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara three times.
They burned incense, scattered flowers, and prostrated themselves in supplication,
repenting and reproaching themselves for all their grave offenses committed throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas;
in a single moment of thought, these were all extinguished, purifying their body, speech, and mind.
At that time, one should recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times— three sets of seven—
during the six periods of the day and night, from the first day until the seventh,
and continuing up to the twenty-first day.
To those of dull faculties who have not yet attained the first fruit,
I at that time bestow the first, second, third, or even the fourth fruit, according to their respective capacities and stages of progress.
Furthermore, for those bodhisattvas who wish to attain the realization of the grounds but are hindered and fail to advance, [I provide the necessary assistance].
One who practices according to the Dharma shall immediately realize the stages as previously described in the Net of Dharma.
I shall now proclaim these dhāraṇī phrases within this trichiliocosm.
Among them, all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śakras, Brahmās, the Four Heavenly Kings, the various ṛṣis,
and the nāga kings fully witness and certify that his great vows have been accomplished;
that the fruit of his aspirations is not in vain, and that it is truly thus.
Fourth, the Bodhisattva Āryavimalakīrti (I-jiu-duo) wished to proclaim a great dhāraṇī named Anagijira— translated in the Jin language as "Savior from All Sickness and Suffering"—
which eliminates all toxic medicines and delivers sentient beings.
To emerge from birth and death;
to deliver those not yet delivered and to bring peace to those not yet at peace;
and to cause those who have not attained nirvana to attain nirvana.
This dharani phrase was spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas of the past; I now wish to speak it:
Amalate, Anābhalate, Kujinade, Kimanade, Kottabhadrade, Agmaliṇade, Vajrapiṇade, Uṣṭhukude, Bhaṭṭarakiṇade, Usunārade, Dharmalate, svāhā. Recite this mantra three times.
Tie six knots made of five-colored threads around both shoulders.
When I now recite these dharani phrases,
all sentient beings within this trichiliocosm— whatever exists therein— [shall hear them].
All karmic offenses, defilements, calamities, evils, and grave illnesses—
by means of the resonance of my Dharma-voice shaking the trichiliocosm—
are dispersed and enter the pores and the six sense faculties of all sentient beings.
May all the oppressive, scorching, and toxic vapors of present illness and suffering,
as well as the burning afflictions and fetters of past karma,
be entirely extinguished without any remainder.
Furthermore, there are practitioners who feel weary of and seek detachment from the three realms;
though they desire to find the essential means of liberation, they are unable to do so.
I shall provide them with immeasurable skillful means.

Should there be neighboring enemies in that land who wish to invade and oppress it,

At that time, the king should feel shame and remorse,
reproaching himself and offering his apologies to the myriad people.
He should bathe thoroughly in purity and put on new, clean garments.
Whether on a high tower or within a palace,
one should burn incense, scatter flowers, and pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
At that time, one should three times call my name, "Bodhisattva Jiu-tuo" (Savior-Deliverer).
"I now take refuge" is said three times.
At that time, one should immediately recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times—three sets of seven—in whichever direction a thief is approaching.
At that time, there shall be eight classes of spirits and deities who will rain down sand,
gravel, and stones, unleashing great black winds, thunder, and lightning,
like the collapse of heaven, shaking the earth and the heavens.
At that time, the hostile bandits naturally retreated and dispersed.
Such is the supernatural power of me, the Bodhisattva Jīvaka, in rescuing and liberating sentient beings.
Fifth, I, the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla, wish to proclaim a great dhāraṇī.
These dhāraṇī phrases were spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas of the past.
I now wish to speak of a dhāraṇī named Anagidhilu— translated into Chinese as "Delivering Sentient Beings."
The sufferings of old age, illness, and death, as well as the sufferings of the three miserable realms—may all these present illnesses of sentient beings be completely relieved.

*Anajipha dzou | Kshurapha dzou | Chipulupha dzou | Anasukahadupha dzou | Ushakimparakapha dzou | Giruvanapha dzou | Haryahudenuvapha dzou | Girmaphulidinnapha dzou | Usutirupha dzou | Girbambhapha dzou | Aparidinnapha dzou | Husatupha dzou | Girmalidinnapha dzou | Svāhā.* Recite this mantra five times. This mantra can cause earth to take on the appearance of water and water to take on the appearance of earth;

it is transformed into the characteristic of non-form.
If, within this trichiliocosm, there are practitioners whose four great elements are out of harmony,

There are sentient beings who are entangled, enveloped, and bound by the defilements of their past karmic offenses,

It is incinerated and purified to bring one out of the triple world;

Those who seek nobility, those who seek intelligence,
those who seek dhāraṇī, those who seek wisdom,
and those who wish to behold the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Facing him, he received a prediction;
he wished to see me, the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla,
and was granted the four fruits of śrāmaṇya.
If one wishes to end this life and be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven to behold Maitreya,
or wishes to be born in the pure Buddha-lands of other directions in the presence of currently living Buddhas,
one should copy, recite, and practice this dhāraṇī.
While dwelling on the ground of having few desires, being content, and purely maintaining the precepts,
one should always cultivate a sense of shame and remorse, practicing straightforward conduct,
and exert oneself diligently without fail throughout the six periods of day and night.
One must not allow the five pungent vegetables, wine, or meat to pass one's lips.
By practicing with such diligence for one hundred and fourteen days, one’s inner and outer realms will become transparent and clear;
facing the Buddhas of the ten directions, one will behold them face-to-face and receive their prediction of enlightenment.
"Good son, after the passing of such a number of kalpas,
you shall attain Buddhahood with a land such as this,
a community of disciples such as this, and a lifespan such as this."
If a śrāvaka seeks the four fruits,
they too should practice this dhāraṇī in this same manner; its efficacy is equal and no different,
though there are distinctions in what is realized according to the sharpness or dullness of their faculties.
The dhāraṇī phrases spoken by me, Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla,
possess such supernatural power that they are true and not false.
Sixth, I, the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, wish to speak a great dhāraṇī named *Aṇāgacchi* (in the language of Jin, "Saving All from the Suffering of Disease").
It severs all nets of doubt, extracts the poisonous arrows of the four perversions, and causes one to emerge from the triple world.

*Gīvaṭanate asuparati ghoḍuparati asutaparati unahuparati jomuyaparati dhughoḍuparati jomuyaparati svāhā.* Recite this mantra three times; tie three knots with thread of three colors and fasten it around the neck.
This dhāraṇī mantra was spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas;

The power of this dhāraṇī can cause the earth of the trichiliocosm to quake and split open,
so that the sentient beings therein spontaneously leap forth.
At that time, I immediately employ the power of wisdom.
At that time, they receive him and place him in one spot;
they then wash away his defilements with the cool water of meditative concentration,
rub and wipe him clean, and comfort his mind.
For example, it is like a bhikṣu entering the third dhyāna;
thereafter, according to whether their faculties are sharp or dull,
those who are destined to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi [shall do so].
According to their respective stages, he bestowed everything upon them;
if there were śrāvakas who were to attain the four fruits of the śramaṇa,
he bestowed them in succession so as to fulfill their aspirations.
There are practitioners who transcribe and recite these dhāraṇī phrases;
[thereby they eliminate] the four hundred and four diseases within their present bodies,
as well as the offenses of violating the precepts, the five heinous crimes, and all hindrances to the Path.
All karmic misfortunes from past lives shall be completely extinguished without remainder.
By the power of my majestic spiritual authority as the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta,
the practices cultivated by this practitioner shall become increasingly superior and all shall be fully accomplished.
There are practitioners who, in whatever place they are born, attain the knowledge of past lives;
they penetrate a hundred births, a thousand births, and hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of births without obstruction,
as clearly as if observing an *āmalaka* fruit in the palm of their hand.
One who wishes to attain the dhāraṇīs of hearing and retaining, and the dhāraṇī of revolving;
one who wishes to attain the four analytical knowledges for unimpeded preaching of the Dharma;
and one who wishes to attain the ten powers and four fearlessnesses of a Buddha.
If you wish to cultivate the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics of a Buddha so that they may be swiftly accomplished;
if you wish to attain the Vajra-samādhi, transcend the ten stages, and enter the true rank of a Buddha.
One should copy, recite, and practice this dhāraṇī.
Day and night, during the six periods, one must never neglect or forget it.
One should purely maintain the ground of the precepts, refraining entirely from eating the five pungent roots, alcohol, meat, or fish.
By practicing fewness of desires, contentment, and upright conduct,
and by cultivating this dhāraṇī,
no non-human being shall be able to cause them affliction or disturbance.
At that time, I shall go together with Śakra, Brahmā,
and the Four Great Kings to the place where this person dwells to comfort their mind,
causing their practice to increase and expand day by day.
Seventh, I, the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, wish to proclaim a great dhāraṇī named Oṣadhivimukti— translated in the Jin language as "Saving All from the Suffering of Disease"—

May all practitioners attain [liberation] through the ten thousand practices.

*Anaji zhilou* (阿那耆置樓), *Boluodina ji zhilou* (波羅帝那耆置樓), *Ruomaduo luo ji zhilou* (若摩陀羅耆置樓), *Ashuotuo luo ni ji zhilou* (阿輸陀羅尼耆置樓), *Wusuopozhi nashe zhilou* (烏穌波置那奢置樓), *Hulubopozhi naji zhilou* (胡盧波置那耆置樓), *Zhapofupozhilou* (遮波副波置樓), *Ruowuli zhibo zhilou* (若無梨置波置樓), *Fufuhulizhibo zhilou* (浮浮呼梨置波置樓), *Ruowuazhe bulidilou* (若無阿遮不梨帝樓). *Svāhā*. These dharani phrases were spoken by forty billion buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River,
in the past; I have now spoken them.
The power of this dhāraṇī can cause the ten buddha-worlds to tremble in six ways.

by virtue of my own great power and majestic spiritual authority,
as well as by the majestic spiritual authority of this dhāraṇī.

He burns away and washes clean the karmic defilements and hindrances to the Path, causing them to awaken;
he causes all to resolve upon the mind of Bodhi.
There were practitioners whose four elements were out of harmony and who were afflicted by the suffering of illness.
If there be anyone who can read and recite this dhāraṇī,

The wish-fulfilling jewel causes nothing to be lacking.
By my supernatural power and the power of this dhāraṇī, these sons and daughters of good family [shall attain this].
Because they redouble their diligence, they immediately attain the great fruit.
Eighth is I-kien-yung Bodhisattva, who wishes to proclaim a great dhāraṇī named Anajichih-lou—translated into Chinese as "Rescuing and Delivering Sentient Beings."
He delivers sentient beings from the suffering of birth and death and rescues those impoverished within the three realms, like the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi;
he is also like a king who unties the bright jewel from his topknot and bestows it upon the poor.
It is just as a compassionate father shows his son a treasure trove;
the power of this dhāraṇī is likewise.

If there is no *hupatthilu*, *usutathilu*, *nakithilu*, *usuhunakithilu*, *vatusathilu*, *viridhanathilu*, *usakhinathilu*, *chabuhusuthathilu*, *namithathilu*, *achibuthilu*, or *viridhanathilu*, *svāhā*—recite this mantra three times, tie it with thread of three colors, make seven knots, and bind them to the site of the pain.
This dharani phrase was spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas of the past; I now speak it.
There may be kings whose kingdoms experience irregularities in water and drought, such that the grain does not ripen.
At that time, one should recite this dhāraṇī seventy-seven times and invoke my name, "Bodhisattva Firm Courage," three times.

I shall then command the great dragon Anavatapta and the dragon Sāgara to dispatch all the minor dragons to provide sufficient water, causing the country to become prosperous and abundant. If epidemics should spread within the kingdom...
When there are sentient beings whose bodies are afflicted by the calamities of illness and suffering,
I shall at that time go to those people and provide medical treatment and relief according to their specific ailments.
There are sentient beings who lack material wealth;
I shall provide for them so that they have nothing lacking.
If there are kings who wish to fulfill their aspirations, [I shall grant them].
One should practice this dhāraṇī.
Whether in a stūpa or in a secluded place,
one should bathe until clean and put on fresh, pure clothing.
For seven days and seven nights, observe the eight precepts.
Practice the Way during the six periods of the day,
reciting this dhāraṇī seven times during each period.
If the king’s mind is pure and sincere,
he shall obtain his wish within three days and three nights;
even if it takes up to seven days, there will be no failure to achieve the result.
Burn black aloeswood and white sandalwood incense;
scatter five-colored flowers and light lamps of sesame oil on the eighth,
fourteenth, and fifteenth days of the month.
At that time, if they three times call upon my name,
"Vīravīrya Bodhisattva," I shall then go with the eight classes of devas,
nāgas, and others to that person's location and grant their wish.
If this person, whether in a dream or with a fully awakened mind, obtains precious jewels, sees a white elephant, or obtains fruit, one should know at that time that their wish has been fulfilled.

Homage to Avalokiteśvara, whose voice is like a lion’s roar and fearless, whose voice is great compassion and gentle softness, whose voice is the pure clarity of Great Brahmā, whose voice is the great light that shines everywhere, whose voice is that of a celestial hero, who is able to bestow happiness upon sentient beings and deliver them from the shore of birth and death.

The Dharani of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva: Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Tathāgata kuli kuli thuta thuta. Bhadrāsme bhara-harata. Svāhā. If one recites this dharani three times every morning, all things will be auspicious.

The *Ākāśagarbha-dhāraṇī*: *Namo buddhāya*. *Tudubuddha mahāmoggallāna svatthidha*. *Yari kili mili mihavali*. *Sarvaga yimili sarvagamili svāhā*. This dhāraṇī of twelve lines also appears on the third leaf of the second fascicle; it was absent from the Danben (the "Cinnabar" manuscript), so it has been removed from that version as a duplication. Recite this eight hundred times while burning fine aloeswood incense so that the smoke does not cease.
To obtain blessings for others, one must use eight hundred yellow flowers.
If it be a son of good family, his present body shall be at peace;
whatever he seeks in his heart, he shall obtain without exception.
If it be a woman, she shall be transformed into a man.

Those who are able to practice this path with a sincere heart for one day and one night across six periods, reciting and upholding it, shall eliminate the sins of three kalpas and never again enter the evil realms.
It should be practiced during the cool seasons of spring and autumn: specifically during the third month, the eighth month, the fourth month, and the ninth month.
At other times, it is not so.

Gaganagañja Bodhisattva Dhāraṇī: *tadyathā | amija amija | kāruṇika | cara cara | sañcara | vicara | kāruṇika | ramu ramu | vikāta-ye | mama punaḥ śamane | kāruṇika | cintāmaṇi | puraye | kāruṇika | sadhāśamata-pāda-aryatari-phakuruti-vipika-phakku | cirudhi-vipikaka-phakku-kāruṇika | kāruṇika | phurita-duma-aśa | sattva-paripācaka-ākāśati | svāhā.* If there are sentient beings with various kinds of illnesses...

they are deaf, blind, mute, or speech-impaired, with their sense faculties incomplete;

I, the Bodhisattva Śakramana,
now wish to proclaim a great divine mantra to protect all sentient beings.

whether bandits, thieves, or pestilence— shall be utterly extinguished.

He bestowed compassion upon the world, showing leniency toward all people and things.

Through repentance and shame, he began anew with the people.
From this day forward, all evils shall cease throughout the day and night, and all manner of goodness shall gather universally.
The devas and nāgas shall rejoice, sending down rain in its proper season;
the five grains shall ripen to maturity, and pestilential vapors shall be extinguished.
At that time, the King should recite this dhāraṇī three times each day;
his aspirations will be fulfilled, truly and not in vain.
Thus spoke the Bodhisattva Śreṇika, son of the Śākyas,
exhorting all kings on matters of state.

*Jñānabhadra*: In the language of China, this means "awakening those who are slumbering in the long sleep of birth and death. *Vajrabhadra*: In the language of China, this means "lifting up sentient beings who lie in the mire of the five desires. *Pilindavatsa*: In the language of China, this means "I now extract [them] by the power of this dhāraṇī, for sentient beings have been struck by ignorance, greed, and hatred."
It enables sentient beings to attain liberation of mind;
ultimately, they abide in the One Vehicle and do not fall into the Lesser Vehicle,
becoming ultimately pure, perfect, and complete.

just as turbid water becomes clear when a divine jewel is placed within it.

wherever the influence of this dhāraṇī reaches,
sentient beings receive its blessings and all attain liberation.
By this dhāraṇī mantra,

wondering, "Whose supernatural transformation is this that has reached such an extent?
All the palaces of the nāga kings are utterly shaken."
Trembling with anxiety like a tree shaken by the wind,
the various dragons were startled and fled, hiding in their burrows;
the minds of the various immortals and seers were bewildered and their brains spun.

the waters of the four great oceans surged and boiled,

This dhāraṇī can eliminate the great sins of the five heinous acts and the cycle of birth and death for ten billion kalpas.
If there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite it,
they shall never fall into the three miserable realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals.
For what reason? When the Buddhas of the past were about to enter *nirvāṇa*, they invariably spoke of this, honoring, extolling, and admiring it;
they praised its merit as being immeasurable and entrusted it to the bodhisattvas.
In the future, there will be sentient beings who hear this dhāraṇī;
those who cultivate it with a focused mind will receive immeasurable rewards for their merit,
like Mount Sumeru or a sea of jewels.
Ordinary beings are unable to measure it.
If there are those who commit various evil deeds and merely hear the name of this dhāraṇī in secret, yet fail to practice it, [they will still attain benefit].
If one harbors this single [thought] in the heart, one will fall into hell;
yet within all the hells, the pains shall not be inflicted due to the grace of this person.
There are those who, through diligent practice in their present body, are able to attain it.
One beholds hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddha-fields.
The merit obtained is immeasurable and cannot be fully described;
only the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are able to exhaustively fathom it.
Those of the two vehicles, the śrāvakas, are unable to know it.
Why is this? This dhāraṇī was not spoken by one Buddha or two Buddhas.
This was spoken by Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the past.
At that time, having obtained this sutra,
I immediately ceased begging for food and joyfully headed toward my cave.
Upon reaching the cave, he burned incense, prostrated, and praised [the deity] with tears of sorrow.
He practiced recitation and chanting within the cave for one year;
only then was he able to do so, because his karmic obstacles had previously hindered him.
I could not bring myself to enter his heart.
At that time, during the night of an autumn month,
I bathed and practiced the path for seven days.
Just as there were many who were confused when a youth first began his training,
so too was it for another seven days; he remained in that same state of confusion without difference,
his heart filled with grief and distress, not knowing what to do.
I calmly contemplated the syllables of this dhāraṇī within my mind;
after several repetitions, my mind suddenly became settled.
At that time, I was filled with joy, like a person who finds hundreds of thousands of catties of gold in the earth.
No one knew of this, yet my inner joy did not cease; it was the same for me at that time.
After practicing for several years, my flight became unimpeded, and I beheld the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
In the future, there will be practitioners who perform these rites according to the Dharma. I, Mañjuśrī,
now wish to proclaim a divine mantra.
To deliver all sentient beings and eliminate the root of their lustful desire,
there is a mantra named Usuka— translated into Chinese as "Eliminating Lustful Desire and Dispelling Arrogance."

Kūli kūlideṇa | Ucchu ucchudeṇa | Dhūhu dhūhudeṇa | Kuṭṭha kuṭṭhadeṇa | Yamidu yamidu deṇa | Kuṭṭahu kuṭṭahu deṇa ucchu ucchu deṇa | Yamija yamija deṇa | Dhūhuṭṭha kuṭṭha ta svāhā. Recite this mantra three times; tie seven knots in a thread and bind it to the feet.
This mantra can cause those who have lost their minds to regain right mindfulness;
it extinguishes the fire of lust so that the mind attains clarity and coolness;
it removes one's pride and extinguishes the fires of the fetters and proclivities.
The defilements and obstacles of the three poisons are all completely eliminated.
If women or virtuous men find their spirits dwelling in the deep abyss of ignorance, [they shall be delivered].
Having long dwelt within birth and death, they are unable to find the essential way out.
Sinking in the swirling currents of the stream of birth and death and drowning in the ocean of lustful desire,
none are able to awaken them, and none know how to seek the essential way out.
Alas, how deeply lamentable!
If a son or daughter of good family attains awakening of mind and comes to feel revulsion for sensual desire.
One should cause them to read and recite this dhāraṇī mantra;
thus, the fire of lust will gradually be extinguished.
Once lust is extinguished, pride will naturally perish of its own accord.
Once pride has been extinguished, the mind becomes concentrated;
once the mind is concentrated, the fetters and latent tendencies are entirely extinguished;
once the fetters and latent tendencies are extinguished, the mind attains liberation.
Once the mind is liberated, one immediately attains the fruit of the Path.
This is what is called the power of the great divine mantra.
Its truth is sincere and not false; such is the power of its spiritual efficacy.
Abstain from alcohol and the five pungent roots for seven times seven, or forty-nine days.
One must not eat any kinds of impure meat.
If the practitioner is a man, he should observe this for nine times nine, or eighty-one days.
If a woman practices this, she should do so for seven times seven, forty-nine days;
furthermore, during the six periods of the day and night,
she should diligently recite with a focused mind and burn black aloeswood and white sandalwood incense.
He scattered flowers as an offering to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
He recited the scriptures during the six periods of the day without ever neglecting or forgetting them.
Once the prescribed number of days was completed, his fetters were immediately extinguished.
His mind is serene and free from further lustful desire.
I, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
now wish to proclaim the name of a great divine mantra.
It eliminates all malevolent spirits, ghosts, as well as demonic and heterodox sorcery.

There is a mantra named *Udāyī-dharaṇī* (in the language of Jin, it means "Eliminating the Illnesses of Beings and Purifying the Five Viscera, Six Bowels, and Triple Burner"). By means of the water of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-samādhi*), it washes and moistens them, cleansing and purifying them like vermilion being rinsed.

Humo-jiedi-zhou, husumo-jiedi-zhou, wujue-bili-jiedi-zhou, jujue-midi-jiedi-zhou, wuxiami-jiedi-zhou, shapi-ruo-jiedi-zhou, woxianmi-jiedi-zhou, mijia-dudijiedi-zhou, juer-wusuodijiedi-zhou, weiran-mijia-duwusuodijiedi-zhou, bilidina-jiedi-zhou. Svāhā. Recite this mantra seven times; make seven knots in a thread and tie them around the ankles (or, according to the Dan version, the knees).
This great divine mantra can cause the practitioner’s mind to attain purity, free from all diseases;
the mind attains liberation, and wisdom attains liberation.
It neutralizes all toxic medicines and eliminates all afflictions and calamities;
all malevolent spirits and demons will be utterly extinguished.
As it is for one person, so it is for many; one should recite and chant this until it is thoroughly mastered.
In every place and at every time, for the sake of all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa, I have bound this divine mantra.
It shall cure all malevolent spirits and enchantments and neutralize all toxic drugs;
it must be circulated and spread throughout the entirety of Jambudvīpa.
This is due to the meager merit of sentient beings in the age of the Dharma’s decline;
there are none who are not afflicted by these various heterodoxies.
One must diligently teach them to read and recite so that all may come to understand.
I, the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of Concentration,
have now come from the world of Wondrous Joy for the sake of the sentient beings of this Sahā world in the five turbidities,
in order to eliminate the obstacles to meditative concentration.
He eradicates the darkness of ignorance,
opens the eye of wisdom,
and bestows the water of meditative concentration.
Washing away the defilements and obstacles of the mind,
one plants the sprout of bodhi;
it gradually grows lush and tall.
He opens and reveals the gates of the Three Vehicles and demonstrates their fruit and true nature.
There is a mantra named *Gucchi-dou*— in the Jin language, it means "Summoning Illumination"— which dispels black darkness, eliminates sins, and removes the defilements of the eye of wisdom.
If midī-tu, uśuna-tu, kuyā-tu, gomaru-tu, uyemi-tu, husupudha-tu, ukimi-tu, husina-tu, usukudi-tu, svāhā. Recite this mantra three times.
Tie three knots made from thread of five colors around the feet.
The power of this great divine mantra extends throughout Jambudvīpa;
if any practitioners wish to cultivate meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), [they should do so].
Or those who are afflicted by the host of heavenly Māras and various malevolent spirits and enchantments:
because of these demonic afflictions, various circumstances arise,
and external evil associates come vying to harass them.
Because of this harassment, internal evils arise once more:
the pursuit of fame, profit, and sustenance; flattery, crookedness, and envy;
and arrogance and haughtiness gather within the mind.
At that time, the practitioner should reproach himself:
"I have acted unwholesomely and am bound by Māra.
Feeling shame and self-reproach, he should lower his head in humiliation.
All Buddhas and the multitude of worthy sages:
throughout past kalpas, I fell into the great hells, the realms of animals and hungry ghosts,
and wandered through the six destinies in a swirling torrent, repeatedly undergoing birth and death.
Now, having obtained a human body with dull faculties and little wisdom,
one desires to cultivate meditative concentration but is unable to attain it,
being shrouded and obscured by the various fetters and afflictions.
"I would rather now shatter my body into dust than ever again be obscured by these fetters and afflictions. Having made this vow,
he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground.
I take refuge in all the Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions— the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
May they forgive my transgressions and eliminate my sins.
Wash my eye of wisdom so that it may become clear and pure;
cleanse the defilements of my mind with the water of compassion,
illuminating my heart until it is transparent and pristine within and without.
Having repented in this way, he again threw himself upon the ground.
Thus he repeated this three times, rising each time to strike his head in prostration.
Having finished repenting and having purified his body and speech, he withdrew and sat down.
Recite this divine mantra twenty-one times.

At that time, you should invoke my name, Samādhi-vaśavartin-rāja Bodhisattva, three times to repent for your transgressions and faults; having spoken thus three times, contemplate with single-minded concentration.
At each and every moment, they repent and reproach themselves;
for hundreds of billions of eons, according to whether their faculties are sharp or dull,
the karmic obstructions of heavy evil deeds have darkened the path.
All malevolent spirits, bewitching demons, celestial Māras,
and sinful defilements shall be completely extinguished without remainder.
At that time, I shall go to that person's dwelling together with a great assembly of Bodhisattvas.
According to the sharpness or dullness of their faculties, he reveals the signs of realization.
This divine mantra spoken by the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of Certainty and Mastery is truthful and not false; its spiritual power is such as this.
I, the Bodhisattva Subhāṣitanetra,
have now come from the land of the Buddha Candrasūryapradīparāja to this Sahā world.
For the sake of the great arhats who wish to attain the first dhyāna, the three knowledges, and the six supernormal powers,
I shall now proclaim a divine mantra so that they may swiftly achieve them.
He eliminates the stains of habitual tendencies and fetters,
as well as subtle and slight obstacles,
thereby purifying his divine eye supernormal power.
The habitual tendencies of the knowledge of past lives,
the clear comprehension of the minds of others, and all future events.
The name of the land,
as well as the assembly of disciples,
and the duration of his lifespan in kalpas.
As well as all matters of supernormal powers,
they hear with penetrating faculty of the ear the affairs of a hundred Buddha-worlds.
With the supernormal power of the body, one is able to fly;
even stone mountains present no obstruction.
This is achieved by extinguishing sensation, perception, and mental formations.
The explanation of the exhaustion of outflows is now complete.

There is a divine mantra named *Oṃ ambaḍilu*—in the language of Jin, this means "the total exhaustion of all burdens"—which is endowed with the three types of clear knowledge (*trividyā*), the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), and the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*).

*Mminnāgahatilo osutahatilo yamitilo uzhuhatilopajihatilopasuhatilakujhuhatiloujamitilakujhuhatile svāhā.* Recite this mantra three times; using thread of three colors, tie six knots and fasten it around the neck.
This great divine mantra is able to cause the practitioner to sever and eliminate habitual tendencies.
Furthermore, they wash away the defilements that obstruct the Path,
purifying the three types of supernormal knowledge and the six higher faculties.
One should recite it and master it thoroughly.
I am the Bodhisattva Adorned with the Marks of Merit.
I have now come from the land of Amitābha Buddha.
I now wish to encourage and assist you so that you may become a bodhisattva,
instructing you in a hundred merits through skillful means.
In order that they may swiftly attain the first stage and be endowed with all the marks and signs of excellence,
he teaches them to practice through exquisite skillful means.
What is meant by "exquisite"?
First, their merit is vast and expansive as they universally compassionately regard all sentient beings.
Second, they provide shelter and protection for all, like a mother’s love for her child, never seeing their faults.
Third, they accumulate virtue and perform good deeds without reckoning the toil.
Fourth, they diligently cultivate the wisdom of equanimity and further transform others through their vigor.
Fifth, they practice the ten wholesome actions and further instruct sentient beings.
Sixth, they maintain the precepts with such purity as a bright pearl.
Seventh, they are transparent both internally and externally, free from any flaw or defilement.
Eighth, the verbal instructions issued from their physical, vocal, and mental actions take compassion as their foundation.
Ninth, whatever deeds they perform, they prioritize the salvation and relief of others.
Ninth, he constantly uses subtle and wondrous skillful means to preach the Dharma for the multitude with a serene and joyful countenance, never contravening their intentions.
Tenth, he constantly travels through various kingdoms to serve as a great preceptor to the nations.
To bear the burden of sentient beings and encompass all things with a mind free from weariness—
this is called the ten great sublime practices undertaken at the time of first generating the aspiration to ascend to the first stage of a bodhisattva.
In this way, ten times ten constitute the hundred merits that produce each of the marks and signs.
I have now explained this briefly;
I shall now recite a mantra so that it may be swiftly accomplished.

There is a mantra named Dhāmaluki (in the language of Jin, meaning "Accomplishing the Adornments of the Marks and Signs, Meritorious Virtues, Severing Habitual Tendencies, and Extinguishing Obstructive Sins").

Atidhamalu, Kutadhamalu, Cidudhamalu, Pajudhamalu, Usadhamalu, Jamidhadhamalu, Utadhamalu, Yamidhadhamalu, Ujodhadhamalu, Hujamikhadhamalu, Pasupasupatidhadhamalu, Ocuocucutidtidhadhamalu, Pasupasupatidhadhamalu, Yurambhiyurambhikadhadhamalu, Japidujapidudhadhamalu. Svāhā. Recite this mantra five times. Take blue thread with two-colored borders, tie it into three knots, and fasten it around the waist.
This mantra can cause the practitioner to adorn themselves with merit and virtue;
endowed with all the primary and secondary marks, they will certainly ascend to the first stage (*bhūmi*).
One should recite it with a diligent mind until it is thoroughly mastered.
Day and night I recite it, never for a moment letting it leave my mind,
and I teach it to other practitioners.
I am the Bodhisattva Suvikhyāta.
I have now come from the land of the Buddha King of the Sound of the Moon of Sublime Tranquility in the northern direction.
In this Sahā world, the Buddha-dharma is about to perish and many people commit evil deeds;
they are greedily attached to gain and offerings, and they constantly engage in mutual criticism and contention.
There is no righteousness between ruler and minister or father and son;
nor is there the ritual propriety between teacher and disciple.
The five turbidities boil like a cauldron, and the three poisons blaze fiercely.
All this is because in previous lives they failed to cultivate virtuous conduct and habitually accumulated various evils.
Now that they have obtained this body, although they possess a human form,
their minds are like those of animals, rākṣasas, or ghosts.
Possessing human bodies yet harboring animal minds, they appear outwardly like members of the human race.
Alas! Amidst such great suffering, as the end of the millennium approaches, there may be but one or two among them who are truly so.
Sentient beings who act erroneously fall into the lower realms;
one should indeed have compassion for these beings.
Now, I wish to speak a mantra to rescue and receive them.
It causes their original practice to be restored to its former state.
There is a mantra called Yunruo midou (in the Jin language, "Extradicating the Root of the Practitioner's Defilements and Washing and Polishing Them to Make Them Pure White").
Ouppharaṭina, chokupharaṭina, yoyomipharaṭina, usudu, cidu, yimidu, kujodu, kujodu, khupadu, svāhā. Recite this mantra three times.
Tie three knots made from threads of two colors, yellow and white, around the neck.
This great divine mantra is like a vast umbrella that provides shade for all,
and like a heavy rain that moistens all.
It is also like a bridge or a boat that carries all across;
among the multitudes of beings within the three realms, there are none who do not rely upon it for their benefit.
Although the secular and the monastic differ in their outward forms, they are one and the same in what they receive and savor.
The myriad species of living beings ultimately converge into the single void.
It is for this reason that Bodhisattvas employ skillful means to adapt their teachings,
acting solely to deliver and liberate all classes of sentient beings.
I now proclaim this mantra for the sake of practitioners,
to rescue and deliver them so that they may swiftly attain the holy fruits of the Three Vehicles.
I command all practitioners to recite it with diligent minds.
This is true and not false; you shall certainly attain the Way.
The Bodhisattva Jewel Moon Radiance now wishes to proclaim a divine mantra to eliminate all karmic offenses incurred during meditative concentration and to remove all defilements and obstructions.
The diseases of the five aggregates and the four great elements are all eliminated.
Sentient beings have not been able to cultivate meditative concentration for immeasurable eons;
therefore, they have long wandered in transmigration, submerged in the ocean of birth and death.
In the swirling currents of the stream of birth and death, none are able to awaken;
out of compassion for these beings, I now wish to proclaim a divine mantra to remove the stains of the three poisons and uproot their feet of ignorance.
Illuminating with the mirror of wisdom and bestowing the water of meditative concentration,
may the sprouts of bodhi grow.
It shall cause one to reach the shore of nirvana.

There is a mantra named *ujja* (in the Jin language, "remover"), which eliminates the defilements of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and repels the sins that obstruct the Path; it is capable of utterly extinguishing all demons and malevolent spirits.

Jamate zhòu, wūtiè zhòu, jùruòtiè zhòu, shātiè zhòu, xiāmìtiè zhòu, wùnángtiè zhòu, jùshātiè zhòu, hūtiè zhòu, svāhā. Recite this mantra three times; take two threads, one yellow and one purple, tie them into eight knots, and bind them to the site of the pain.
This mantra can cause those who have lost their right mindfulness to regain it;
all heavy transgressions committed throughout hundreds of billions of kalpas can be utterly destroyed, leaving nothing remaining.
If there are sentient beings who wish to cultivate meditative concentration,
yet their minds are distracted and darkened so that they do not perceive the objective realm,
and their afflictions arise frequently, being shrouded by sleep;
At that time, this person should think:
"I am shrouded by the obscurations of past karma;
I ought to feel shame and remorse, repent, and reproach myself."
He lit lamps to continue the illumination,
burned incense, and scattered flowers as an offering to all the Buddhas;
having made offerings to the Buddhas, he further made offerings individually.
I, the Bodhisattva Ratnacandraprabha,
lit seven-branch lamps and burned aloeswood incense for seven days and seven nights, diminishing my sleep.
During the six periods of day and night, he deeply reproached himself and confessed his past transgressions.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha knows men and perceives men;
he clearly sees the characteristics of the offenses committed by his disciples.
The Buddhas of the ten directions, the great Bodhisattvas,
Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings all bear witness to this;
they clearly perceive the characteristics of the transgressions I have committed.
I now repent, and may you all bear witness to this.
May my transgressions be extinguished without remainder.
Having thus completed the repentance at each respective time, I pray for their total purification.
Recite this divine mantra seven times and then cease.
Having recited it seven times, sit in silence.
Contemplate with single-minded concentration; in this way, these defilements of sin shall gradually be eliminated.
As their minds become increasingly concentrated, their spheres of perception become clear.
Those with sharp faculties will, within three, four,
or even seven days, behold me, the Bodhisattva Jewel Moon Radiance.
Having removed obstacles and extinguished transgressions, he bestows the fruit upon them.
For those of dull faculties, this takes two, three, or seven weeks;
for those of extremely dull faculties, it takes seven weeks—forty-nine days.
There are those who attain meditative concentration and those who attain the fruits [of the path], and they never pass their time in vain.
Such is the power of this great divine mantra.
I am the Bodhisattva Beichen, named Miaojian.
Now I wish to proclaim a divine mantra to protect all lands;
its deeds are most extraordinary, and thus it is named "Wondrous Vision.
It dwells within Jambudvīpa.
The most excellent among the multitude of stars,
the immortal among immortals,
the great general of the bodhisattvas.
The Bodhisattvas of Radiant Eyes extensively save all living beings.

There is a great divine spell named Guna-paryanta (in the Jin language, "Protecting the Realm"), which assists various kings; there is nothing for the elimination of calamities and the repelling of enemies that does not depend upon it.

Gūḍe tustuṣṭa, arjumiṭṭha, uduttha, gujaṭṭha, parādiṭṭha, yamiyaṭṭha, uduttha, kurodiṭṭha, jamadha, svāhā. Recite this mantra five times; tie it with thread of seven colors into three knots and bind them to the site of pain.
This great divine mantra was spoken by as many Buddhas of the past as there are grains of sand in forty Ganges Rivers.
In the past, I heard the exposition of this great divine mantra’s power from those Buddhas.
From that time onward, for seven hundred kalpas, he has resided in Jambudvīpa as a great national preceptor.
He has presided over the four continents as the king among the stars,
attaining supreme sovereignty over the four continents.
I shall take charge of all matters of state.
If various kings do not employ their ministers according to the True Dharma,
and their hearts lack shame and remorse;
I am able to remove this tyrant who, through arrogance, vacuity, turbidity, and disorder,
has unleashed his various ministers to cruelly oppress the common people;
I shall summon the worthy and capable to replace him upon the royal throne.
If one can feel shame and remorse to reform evil and cultivate goodness;
if one can embrace those who do good and distance oneself from those who are evil;
and if one's mind is vast and expansive, universally compassionate toward all.
To provide shelter and rescue is like a bridge or a boat;
to embrace all people and things is like parents.
When the state possesses men of talent and ability, they should be summoned and enlisted.
He revered the worthy and honored the sages as if looking upon his own parents.
The King personally attended the court to adjudicate affairs,
treating the people and their possessions without partiality, like a clear mirror.
If the king can cultivate these virtues— reforming his past ways and cultivating the future,
repenting for sins previously committed, feeling shame and self-reproach,
and lamenting his transgressions and faults— then [he shall attain such merit].
Having repented and reproached oneself, one should cultivate three virtues:
first, to show reverence toward the Triple Gem;
second, to have compassion for the poor and to provide care and protection for the orphaned and the elderly within the country.
Third, one maintains a mind that is always impartial toward enemies and kin;
one rectifies grievances and wrongs, yet does not oppress the people or their property.
If one can cultivate the various virtues mentioned above, [one shall attain these fruits].
At that time, I shall lead the great celestial kings,
the various Śakras, the Lords of Life, the Commanders of the Celestial Courts, and the Ministers of the Heavenly Bureaus,
to eliminate death, ensure birth, diminish transgressions, increase merit, augment the life-span, and prolong one's years.
He informed the various celestial offices to dispatch one thousand seven hundred benevolent deities to patrol and guard the borders of the kingdom and protect the land,
eliminating all calamities and extinguishing all wickedness.
The winds and rains were timely, and the grains ripened in abundance.
Pestilence was eliminated, and there were no powerful enemies.
The people lived in peace and happiness, praising the virtue of the king.
If this king can also practice the recitation of this dhāraṇī,
it will be like a Wheel-Turning Sage King who has obtained a wish-fulfilling jewel;
the divine power of that jewel will subdue and eliminate all calamities and misfortunes.
By the power of this great divine mantra, all the virtues mentioned above can be accomplished; the extinguishing and elimination of calamities and evils is likewise so.
You should know that the power of this great divine mantra is like a king’s bright jewel, and it is also just like this.
I am the Rishi Śvetaketu.
I now wish to proclaim a divine mantra.
I am a rishi endowed with the five supernatural powers who practices the bodhisattva path.
The most excellent among the five planets;
among the immortals and seers,
I am supreme in supernatural powers and radiance.
He presides over the affairs of the four continents as well as those of humans and devas;
he governs the calamities and transformations within the lands,
and the extension or contraction of the lifespan.
The principles of yin and yang and their transformations;
the *tushu* (charts and books) and prophetic records (*chanji*);
and matters of both deceitful falsehood and honest integrity.
I am able to alleviate calamities and eliminate wickedness;
all matters concerning what should be expanded or contracted are fully known to me.
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, I now wish to proclaim a divine mantra and protect their lands.
There is a mantra named Anāhuta; in the language of Jin, it means "Wishing to Protect the Lands and the Sentient Beings of One Quarter of Jambudvīpa."

*Pāṭahupalu, yamamahupalu, yamaduhupalu, ujjhanahupalu, yamihupalu, uzhuhupalu, kujasaha-hupalu, huyoduhupalu, svāhā.* Recite this mantra three times. Take two colors of thread, yellow and white, tie them into two knots, and fasten them around the neck.
This great divine mantra was spoken by as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in three Ganges Rivers in the past. In the past, I...
Having heard this mantra from the various Buddhas,
one hundred kalpas have already passed since that time.
The merit he cultivated was such that none among the immortals could equal it;
internally, he secretly maintained the Mahayana precepts and practices of a bodhisattva,
while externally, he manifested as an immortal.
Having fully completed the cultivation of the pure Dharma-body and the six pāramitās of the bodhisattvas,
he outwardly manifests through skillful means among the immortals and seers.
Although he harmonizes his light with others, he does not share in their defilements;
this is called the bodhisattva’s skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) of taking birth through expedient means.
If there are kings of Jambudvīpa who,
having little merit in their previous lives, dwell in the age of the Dharma’s decline,
yet through some slight roots of goodness have become human rulers.
Their bodies lack the power of merit and their minds are dark with little wisdom;
furthermore, they encounter beings of the five dregs who are dull and turbid—
like a foolish man driving a broken cart with a slow ox.
I saw that they wished to cross a perilous path which was extremely difficult to traverse; having seen this,
I felt compassion and pity for them.
It was to deliver sentient beings who were drowning in suffering and toil;
it was because he wished to lead them forth and enable them to escape their hardships,
while simultaneously rescuing the King from the peril of the slow-moving ox.
Therefore, I now speak this divine mantra.
If the king of the country hears these words,
he will feel shame in his heart and recognize for himself his own meager merit.
Reforming the past and cultivating the future, they give rise to a vast and expansive mind;
with compassion they encompass all, pitying suffering sentient beings,
enduring evil while practicing goodness, and never wronging the people or their possessions.
He shall establish and protect the True Dharma, entrust authority to the worthy and employ the wise;

All [these] were completely extinguished without remainder.

they constantly bathe and observe the fast on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days of the month.
